Haircuts · The difference

Fade vs taper: the difference, and which one to ask for.

Both get shorter toward the neck. A taper does it softly, a fade takes it down to the skin. Here's how to choose.

By The Q JournalPublished Nov 25, 2026

In this guide

The taper: subtle and grown-up

The fade: sharp contrast

Low, mid and high

Skin, bald and drop fades

The low taper fade

What to say in the chair

A taper and a fade both shorten the hair gradually as it moves down the sides and back. The difference is how far they go. A taper leaves some hair at the bottom and keeps the change subtle, usually only at the sideburns and neckline. A fade blends all the way down to very short or bare skin, with a more dramatic contrast.

Quick answer: want clean but conservative, ask for a taper. Want sharp and modern, ask for a fade. Not sure, ask for a low taper fade, the in-between that's become one of the most requested cuts.

The taper: subtle and grown-up

A taper keeps most of the length on the sides and only shortens the edges: the neckline and around the ears. It looks tidy in a boardroom and grows out gracefully, so it can go four weeks between cuts. It suits longer styles, side parts and anyone who doesn't want visible scalp.

The fade: sharp contrast

A fade takes the sides down to very short or skin, blending upward into the longer top. The higher it starts, the bolder it looks. It's crisp and modern but shows growth fast, so most fades need a touch-up every two to three weeks to stay sharp.

Low, mid and high

Height is where the shortest part stops. A low fade stays just above the ear and neckline and is the most versatile. A mid fade starts around the temple and suits most textured tops. A high fade climbs toward the crown for maximum contrast, and works best with short or very structured tops.

Skin, bald and drop fades

A skin or bald fade goes down to bare skin at the bottom. A drop fade curves down behind the ear toward the nape, following the head's shape. A burst fade fans out around the ear and leaves length at the back, which is the cut often paired with a modern mullet.

The low taper fade

It's exactly what it sounds like: a fade kept low and tight to the edges like a taper. You get the clean, sharp outline of a fade around the ears and neckline, with the weight of a taper on the sides. Ask for it with a textured crop or a longer top.

What to say in the chair

Name the type and height, then the shortest length: "Low taper, finish at a 1 at the neckline," or "Mid skin fade, blend into a 3, scissor on top." Say whether you want a natural or squared neckline, and how long you usually go between cuts, so it's built to grow out well.

Questions

What's the difference between a fade and a taper?

A taper shortens the hair subtly at the neckline and sideburns and leaves some length. A fade blends down to very short or bare skin, with more contrast.

Which lasts longer, a fade or a taper?

A taper. It grows out more gradually and can usually go about four weeks, while a fade looks best refreshed every two to three weeks.

Is a low taper fade a fade or a taper?

It's a hybrid: a fade's clean edges kept low and tight around the ears and neckline, with the sides left fuller like a taper.
